mainTopic: Which point in a crop's growth decides its year for מעשרות and שביעית. The גמרא finishes the source for the 'one-third' (שליש) rule, then asks how the rule applies to rice, millet, poppy and sesame.
overview: The גמרא finishes learning the שליש rule for grain by re-reading לשלש ("for three") as לשליש ("for one-third"). It defends this reading by showing that another פסוק already teaches the plain three-year blessing. Next it quotes a משנה: rice, millet, poppy and sesame go by the year in which they took root. רבה lists the usual rules: trees by חנטה, grain and olives by שליש, vegetables by לקיטה. He asks which group these four crops belong to. He answers that they ripen little by little, so the חכמים used rooting to keep each field in one year. אביי objects with a ברייתא about the Egyptian bean: there, piling the crop together and separating from the mix solves the mixed-years problem. רבה replies that this works only for רבי שמעון שזורי, who holds יש בילה. The רבנן hold אין בילה. Finally, שמואל rules like that ברייתא. רבי זירא asks how, since שמואל says only liquids mix. The answer is that שמואל holds a crop's year follows גמר פרי, so all the beans belong to one year anyway.

steps.title: Reading 'for three' as 'for one-third'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proof by re-reading לשלש ("for three") as לשליש ("for one-third"), which teaches the שליש rule for grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't read it as "for three"; read it as "for one-third."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof from a פסוק. It reads the word לשלש as לשליש, so the פסוק now hints that one-third growth is the key moment for grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק talks about produce lasting "for three years." With a small change in vowels, the same letters can say "for one-third." So the פסוק also teaches that grain belongs to the year in which it reached one-third of its growth.

keyTerms.meaning: "Do not read": a way of learning a second meaning from the same letters by reading them with different vowels
One-third of a crop's growth, the deciding stage for grain and olives

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean the plain reading is wrong. The פסוק keeps its simple meaning, and the re-reading adds a second lesson on top of it.

phrases.english: Do not read it "for three,"
phrases.notes: This is the word in ויקרא 25:21, where the sixth year's crop will last "for three years."

phrases.english: but rather "for one-third."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a derivation that began before this section
steps.raayaObject: Grain is assigned to a year by when it reaches one-third growth
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 25:21, with the word לשלש re-read as לשליש

steps.title: The word is needed for its plain meaning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that לשלש is needed to teach its simple meaning, that the sixth year will produce enough for three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that word is needed for itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the re-reading from Step 1. It argues that the word is busy teaching its plain meaning, so it is not free to teach another lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple meaning of the פסוק is a promise: the sixth year's crop will last three years. If the word is needed for that promise, the גמרא asks how it can also be used for the שליש rule.

keyTerms.meaning: For itself, meaning for the פסוק's own plain meaning

phrases.english: But it is needed for itself!
phrases.notes: He means the word is needed to promise that the sixth year's crop lasts three years.

steps.kashyaTarget: Using לשלש to teach the שליש rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A word that teaches its plain meaning is not free to teach a second lesson

steps.title: Another פסוק already teaches the three years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a different פסוק already says the old crop lasts until the ninth year, so לשלש is free for the שליש rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another פסוק is written: "And you will sow in the eighth year, and eat from the old produce until the ninth year."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The next פסוק already shows that the crop lasts three years, so the word לשלש is free to teach the one-third rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sixth year's crop is eaten in the sixth, seventh and eighth years, up to the ninth year's harvest, which makes three years. The next פסוק already says this. The extra hint in לשלש can therefore be used for the שליש rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The שליש rule for grain comes from re-reading לשלש as לשליש. This works because ויקרא 25:22 already teaches the three-year blessing.

phrases.english: Another verse is written:
"And you shall sow in the eighth year,
and eat of the old produce
until the ninth year."

steps.terutzResolutionType: The plain meaning is already taught by another פסוק, which frees the word for a new lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לשלש is needed for the three-year blessing
steps.terutzMaskana: ויקרא 25:22 covers the blessing, so לשלש teaches the שליש rule

steps.title: משנה: rice, millet, poppy and sesame go by rooting
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that these four crops go by the year in which they took root, both for מעשרות and for שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: rice, millet, poppy and sesame that took root before ראש השנה are tithed by the past year and are permitted in שביעית. If not, they are forbidden in שביעית and are tithed by the coming year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a משנה about four special crops. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For these four crops, the deciding moment is rooting (השרשה). If they rooted before ראש השנה, they count as the old year, so they take that year's מעשר and are allowed even if the new year is שביעית. If they rooted after, they belong to the new year.

keyTerms.meaning: They are tithed according to the year that is ending
The seventh year of the cycle, the שמיטה year

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה gives a fourth kind of deciding moment, rooting. It does not match the usual three, which leads straight to רבה's question.

phrases.english: We learned there:
Rice, millet, poppy, and sesame
that took root before Rosh HaShanah
are tithed according to the past year,
and are permitted in the Sabbatical Year.
And if not, they are forbidden in the Sabbatical Year,
and are tithed according to the coming year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: a משנה about crops that go by rooting
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rice, millet, poppy and sesame go by the year in which they took root, for both מעשרות and שביעית

steps.title: רבה lists the three standard rules
steps.stepSummary: רבה lists the deciding stage for each kind of crop: trees by חנטה, grain and olives by שליש, vegetables by לקיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The חכמים said: a tree goes by the forming of its fruit, grain and olives go by one-third growth, and a vegetable goes by its picking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה lists the three known rules for deciding which year a crop belongs to. He is setting up a question about the four crops in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of crop has its own deciding moment. For tree fruit it is the fruit's first forming (חנטה). For grain and olives it is one-third growth, as just learned from the פסוק. For vegetables it is picking (לקיטה).

keyTerms.meaning: The first forming of fruit on a tree

phrases.english: Rabba said: The Sages said:
A tree follows the forming of the fruit,
grain and olives follow one-third growth,
a vegetable follows the picking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lists the standard categories so they can be compared with the משנה in Step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trees go by חנטה, grain and olives by שליש, vegetables by לקיטה

steps.title: Which category do the four crops belong to?
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks which of the three categories the חכמים matched these four crops to, since rooting fits none of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: These crops: whom did the חכמים compare them to?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks his question. The four crops go by rooting, which is not one of the three standard rules, so which group are they part of?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rooting is not חנטה, not שליש and not לקיטה. רבה wants to know which known category the חכמים based this rule on.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom, or like which one
They made them equal, or compared them

phrases.english: These, to whom did the Sages equate them?
phrases.notes: "These" are the rice, millet, poppy and sesame from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the משנה in Step 4 fits the rules listed in Step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which standard category the חכמים matched rice, millet, poppy and sesame to, given that they go by rooting

steps.title: רבה explains: these crops ripen little by little, so the חכמים followed rooting
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers his own question. Because these four crops ripen in small batches over time, the חכמים decided their year by השרשה (taking root).
steps.simpleTranslation: Then רבה said: Because these crops ripen a little at a time, the חכמים went by the time they took root.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question he asked in the last step. He explains why the חכמים used rooting as the deciding stage for these four crops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These crops do not ripen all at once. They are picked bit by bit, some before ראש השנה and some after. If the year went by picking, one field would hold crops from two different years, and people might separate תרומה and מעשרות from one year for the other. Rooting happens at one time for the whole field, so it keeps the whole crop in one year.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said; the speaker comes back with a new answer
In small batches, little by little

phrases.english: Rabba then said:
Since they ripen in small batches,
phrases.notes: Literally 'pieces, pieces.' He means the crop ripens and is picked a bit at a time, not all at once.

phrases.english: the Sages went by the time of rooting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 6 by giving a practical reason instead of matching the crops to one of the three categories.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why rooting was chosen for these four crops.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They ripen little by little, so rooting is used to keep the whole crop in one year and avoid mixing years for מעשרות.

steps.title: אביי asks: why not just pile everything together and separate from the mix
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה. There is a simple way to avoid mixing years: pile the whole crop together and separate from the mixture. Each year's produce would then cover its own year.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Let him pile everything into the middle of his threshing floor. Then he ends up separating תרומה from the new produce in it for the new produce in it, and from the old in it for the old in it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's reason. He says the worry about mixing years can be solved easily, so there was no need for a special rooting rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everything is mixed well, any portion taken out holds new and old crop in the same proportions as the whole pile. So the new part of the תרומה covers the new crop and the old part covers the old crop. That would solve the problem רבה raised without changing which year the crop belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: His threshing floor, the place where the harvested crop is piled
New crop (this year) / old crop (last year)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But let him pile his crop into the middle of his threshing floor,
phrases.notes: He means mix the whole crop together in one pile, so new and old are spread evenly.

phrases.english: and it turns out he separates teruma from the new crop in it
for the new crop in it,

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַיָּשָׁן שֶׁבּוֹ עַל הַיָּשָׁן שֶׁבּוֹ!
phrases.english: and from the old crop in it for the old crop in it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְיִצְבּוֹר גּוֹרְנוֹ לְתוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבה gave in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the rooting rule was needed to stop people from separating from one year for another.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The problem has an easy practical fix, mixing the whole pile, so it cannot be the reason for a special rule.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the Egyptian bean: no separating between years
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא to support his point. It discusses an Egyptian bean planted for seed, where part took root before ראש השנה and part after. One may not separate from one part for the other, because new and old cannot cover each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי בן כיפר said in the name of רבי שמעון שזורי: An Egyptian bean planted for seed, where part of it took root before ראש השנה and part after ראש השנה, one may not separate תרומה and מעשרות from this part for that part. This is because one may not separate תרומה and מעשרות from new for old or from old for new.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts bringing a source for his challenge. This part of the ברייתא sets up the problem: one crop belongs to two different years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This bean has exactly the situation רבה described, part of it in one year and part in the next. The ברייתא first states the basic rule that new and old cannot cover each other. That makes the bean case just like the four crops, which prepares the solution in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it taught in a ברייתא? Used to bring a supporting source
For seed, grown for its beans rather than eaten as a green vegetable

phrases.english: Isn't it taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon Shezuri:
An Egyptian bean that one planted for seed,
phrases.notes: Planted for its beans, not to be eaten as a green vegetable.

phrases.english: part of it took root before Rosh HaShana,
and part of it took root after Rosh HaShana —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין וּמְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: one may not separate teruma and tithes from this part for that part,
because one may not separate teruma and tithes
neither from the new crop for the old
nor from the old crop for the new.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the source that backs up אביי's challenge in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The case setup for אביי's proof: a single crop that is split between two years, where new and old may not cover each other. The solution comes in step 10.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי בן כיפר in the name of רבי שמעון שזורי about the Egyptian bean.

steps.title: The ברייתא's solution: pile it all together and separate from the mix
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the fix for the bean. Pile the whole crop together, so that separating from the mixture covers new for new and old for old. This is exactly what אביי suggested.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he act? He piles everything into the middle of his threshing floor. Then he ends up separating תרומה and מעשרות from the new in it for the new in it, and from the old in it for the old in it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of אביי's proof. The ברייתא uses the very method אביי proposed, so the same fix should work for rice, millet, poppy and sesame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bean crop is split across two years by when each part took root, yet the ברייתא does not change the deciding stage to avoid mixed years; it simply mixes the pile. So אביי asks why the four crops needed a rooting rule to avoid mixed years, when the same easy fix was available.

keyTerms.meaning: How should he act? Introduces the practical solution

steps.whatToRemember: אביי shows from the Egyptian bean that mixing the whole pile solves the problem of crops from two years. That makes רבה's reason for the rooting rule questionable for the four crops.

phrases.english: How should he act?
He piles his crop into the middle of his threshing floor,
and it turns out he separates teruma and tithes

phrases.aramaic: מִן הֶחָדָשׁ שֶׁבּוֹ עַל הֶחָדָשׁ שֶׁבּוֹ,
phrases.english: from the new crop in it for the new crop in it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִן הַיָּשָׁן שֶׁבּוֹ עַל הַיָּשָׁן שֶׁבּוֹ.
phrases.english: and from the old crop in it for the old crop in it.
phrases.notes: אביי's point is left unsaid: if this works for the bean, why not for rice, millet, poppy and sesame?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד הוּא עוֹשֶׂה — צוֹבֵר גּוֹרְנוֹ לְתוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 9 with the solution that proves אביי's point.
steps.raayaObject: That piling the crop together is an accepted fix for a crop split across two years.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the ברייתא about the Egyptian bean.

steps.title: רבה says the ברייתא is only one opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers אביי. The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון שזורי, who holds there is בילה, but the רבנן hold there is no בילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you quoting רבי שמעון שזורי? רבי שמעון שזורי holds there is mixing. But the רבנן hold there is no mixing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back on אביי's proof from the ברייתא. He says that ברייתא only follows one תנא, and the רבנן disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's fix depends on the idea that a pile is evenly mixed, so each portion holds old and new in the right amounts. רבה says only רבי שמעון שזורי assumes that (יש בילה). The רבנן say a pile is not truly mixed (אין בילה), so piling does not solve the problem, and רבה's original approach still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing: the idea that combined items become evenly blended together
There is mixing: we assume the pile is evenly blended
There is no mixing: we do not assume an even blend

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying the ברייתא is wrong. He is saying it reflects only רבי שמעון שזורי's view, and the רבנן, who disagree, are the ones his own explanation follows.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי קָאָמְרַתְּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Are you quoting Rabbi Shimon Shezuri?
phrases.notes: רבה is speaking to אביי. The ברייתא אביי brought was taught in the name of רבי שמעון שזורי.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי סָבַר יֵשׁ בִּילָּה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri holds there is mixing.
But the Sages hold there is no mixing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 9-10 by limiting the ברייתא to one opinion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's proof from the ברייתא of the Egyptian bean
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא assumes יש בילה, which only רבי שמעון שזורי holds. The רבנן hold אין בילה, so the fix of piling does not work for them.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון שזורי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר נחמני quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן כיפר, who taught in the name of רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן כיפר, who said it in the name of רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from שמואל on the ברייתא of the Egyptian bean. He says the הלכה follows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after רבה said the ברייתא is only one view, we learn that שמואל rules like that view. This sets up a question: does שמואל really hold יש בילה?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar
who said it in the name of Rabbi Shimon Shezuri.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא of the Egyptian bean from the last steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical ruling on the ברייתא whose authority was just limited.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows the ברייתא of רבי יוסי בן כיפר in the name of רבי שמעון שזורי: one may pile the Egyptian beans together and separate from the pile.

steps.title: רבי זירא: שמואל holds only liquids mix
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges the report. שמואל elsewhere says nothing has בילה except wine and oil, so how could he rule like someone who holds יש בילה for beans?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: Did שמואל really say this? But שמואל said: Nothing has mixing except wine and oil!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks the ruling just quoted. It seems to contradict another statement of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that only liquids, like wine and oil, truly blend. Solids such as beans do not. If so, he should not follow רבי שמעון שזורי, whose reasoning depends on beans mixing evenly.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (opening a contradiction)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly objected to it:
And did Shmuel really say this?
But didn't Shmuel say:

phrases.aramaic: לַכֹּל אֵין בִּילָּה, חוּץ מִיַּיִן וָשֶׁמֶן!
phrases.english: Nothing has mixing, except wine and oil!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of שמואל quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that שמואל ruled like רבי שמעון שזורי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between two statements of שמואל: ruling like the view of יש בילה for beans, while holding אין בילה for everything except liquids.

steps.title: שמואל's real reason: everything follows full ripening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי זירא forgot another rule of שמואל: everything follows גמר פרי. So שמואל agrees with the ruling for a different reason, not because of בילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He forgot what שמואל said: Everything follows the full ripening of the fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. רבי זירא forgot a different statement of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that the year of a crop is set by when it fully ripens (גמר פרי), not when it took root. All the beans ripen at the same time, so they all belong to one year. Then separating from all of them together is fine, even without בילה. שמואל agrees with the outcome of רבי שמעון שזורי, but not with his reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: It slipped his mind / he forgot

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל rules like the ברייתא of the Egyptian bean in practice. His reason is not בילה, since he holds only liquids mix. His reason is that a crop's year follows גמר פרי, and all the beans ripen together.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a ruling can follow an opinion's practical outcome while resting on a completely different reason.

phrases.english: He forgot this that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי זירא, who forgot this other rule of שמואל.

phrases.english: Everything follows the full ripening of the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reasoning: same practical ruling, based on another principle of the same אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון שזורי because he holds יש בילה, which contradicts his rule that only liquids mix.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל rules this way because everything follows גמר פרי. All the beans ripen together and belong to one year, so no בילה is needed.
